channel.title: The Wilson Times - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Wilson Times (wilsontimes.com)

item.title: Planning board approves new housing projects
item.description: The Wilson Planning and Design Review Board signs off on seven rezonings, but denies one. The rezonings will allow for new subdivisions and income-based apartments.

item.title: AREA ROUNDUP: Rams double up Demons in early season showdown
item.description: Area roundup: Greene Central boys tennis tops Fike, Beddingfield softball splits its first two, several local baseball and softball teams fall, and Hunt track sweeps the Franklinton opener.

item.title: Lewis outlasts Honeycutt to win Jerry Moody Memorial
item.description: Landen Lewis outdueled Kaden Honeycutt in a seven-lead-change battle to win the Jerry Moody Memorial at Southern National, earning $5,000 and a unique pig-themed trophy.

item.title: Appeals court upholds conviction
item.description: N.C. appeals court upholds assault, false imprisonment convictions of Wilson man Travis Ray Mercer, rejecting his ineffective counsel claims as he serves a 23–37 month prison term.

item.title: Iran nuclear bomb bad, Saudi Arabia nuclear bomb good?
item.description: An attorney argues Trump’s bid to end Iran’s nuclear deal while pursuing a Saudi nuclear agreement without key safeguards reveals a dangerous double standard on nuclear weapons.

item.title: Rural America needs to band together against corporate greed
item.description: As farm giants push full automation and squeeze out independent growers, a rural Iowa farmer warns that corporate agritech could empty small towns — and argues only solidarity can protect rural America.

item.title: Thune and Johnson: A tale of two orphans
item.description: Columnist Thomas L. Knapp says John Thune and Mike Johnson show “chutzpah” by invoking Iran threats to demand DHS funding after shielding the agency and Trump from accountability on immigration abuses and war powers.

item.title: Wilson has a seat at the table, but does everyone?
item.description: As Wilson welcomes a $69M downtown ballpark and the new Warbirds team, a local resident asks who truly benefits — and urges concrete steps to include the city’s Black majority.

item.title: Our Opinion: 4 observations from Tuesday's NC primaries
item.description: NC primaries brought lopsided local wins, a better-funded Democrat losing to a local leader, a 2-vote Berger–Page Senate cliffhanger and progressive challengers ousting party moderates.

item.title: Tobacco planting begins with eyes on weather
item.description: As Tyner Farms seeds greenhouses for 550 acres of tobacco, costly heating, last year’s floods and shifting weather patterns show how each season is a high-stakes gamble.
